title: SQL built by string concatenation
hints: Look at how the query text is assembled.
code: pool.query(`SELECT * FROM customers WHERE name ILIKE '%${q}%'`)
cause: Untrusted input is interpolated into SQL (injection).
fix: pool.query('SELECT * FROM customers WHERE name ILIKE $1', [`%${q}%`]) and validate q with Zod.
verify: Injection payload returns 0 rows; test added.

title: Missing await
symptom: Response body is {} instead of the booking.
hints: What does an async function return?
cause: A Promise is serialised, not the resolved value.
fix: const booking = await bookings.findById(id); and wrap handlers so rejections reach the error middleware.
verify: Test asserts body.id equals the created id; no unhandled rejection warnings.

title: Errors returned with status 200
symptom: The frontend shows success when validation failed.
fix: Map errors to 400/404/409/500 in a central error handler.
verify: Tests assert exact status codes for each failure.

title: Missing foreign key, orphan bookings
symptom: Revenue report total is lower than the sum of bookings.
hints: Find bookings whose customer_id does not exist.
code: SELECT b.* FROM bookings b LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.id=b.customer_id WHERE c.id IS NULL;
cause: No FK, so deleted customers left orphan bookings and the INNER JOIN drops them.
fix: Migration: clean/repair orphans, then ALTER TABLE bookings ADD CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT.
verify: Orphan query returns 0; deleting a customer with bookings fails; report matches.

title: Pool client never released
symptom: After about 10 requests the API hangs.
hints: What if an exception is thrown?
cause: The client is never returned to the pool; once max clients are checked out new requests wait forever.
fix: try { ... } finally { client.release() } or use pool.query for single statements.
verify: Load test with 100 requests completes; pool.totalCount/idleCount stable.

title: Price stored as text
fix: Migration: ALTER COLUMN price_cents TYPE integer USING price::integer (after cleaning) with CHECK >= 0.
verify: ORDER BY price_cents returns numeric order; test added.

title: GROUP BY report with duplicate rows
symptom: Each service appears several times in the revenue report.
code: SELECT s.name, sum(s.price_cents) FROM bookings b JOIN services s ON ... JOIN staff_hours h ON h.staff_id=b.staff_id GROUP BY s.name, h.weekday
cause: Joining a one-to-many table (staff_hours) multiplies bookings, and extra grouping columns split the result.
fix: Remove the unnecessary join and group only by service id/name.
verify: One row per service; totals equal manual sum.
